name: gpg
description: GnuPG: OpenPGP encryption, decryption, signing, and key management for files and communications.

flags.description: Symmetric encryption with a passphrase (gpg -c file → file.gpg).
Encrypt for a recipient's public key.

examples.explanation: Symmetric encryption: prompts for a passphrase, produces secrets.txt.gpg. Decrypt with gpg -d secrets.txt.gpg > secrets.txt.
Interactive key pair creation: name, email, passphrase. The public key is shareable; the private key never leaves your machine.
Encrypts so that ONLY alice can decrypt it, using her public key — the heart of public-key cryptography.
Verifies a software download against the developer's signature — the standard integrity check for source releases.

about: GPG supports two modes: symmetric (one shared passphrase) and asymmetric (key pairs: public to encrypt, private to decrypt). Keys live in ~/.gnupg/. Software projects publish release signatures — verifying them confirms the download is untouched.
useCases: Sign your own releases and commits (git uses GPG signing).
mistakes: Losing the private key or passphrase — the data is gone forever; there is no recovery.
Confusing public (share) and private (never share) keys.
warnings: No key, no recovery. Back up private keys securely (gpg --export-secret-keys) before relying on them.
